@Pavel Kalian Thanks for doing the win64 heavy lifting!

My understanding of 5.16 platform support below. Did I get it right?
@Dave Register : Will 5.16 for Android still use wxw 3.0?

5.16 is planned to be released end of March/beginning of April -27. Currently envisioned platform support:

  1. Windows: win64 for x86_64. That is, no 32bits builds
  2. Debian: 13/Trixie and 12/Bookworm . Version 14/Forky will land in summer/autumn -27 at which point we should release 5.16 for it. All released for arm64 and amd64
  3. Ubuntu: 22.04 Jammy, 24.04 noble and 26.04 resolute. There will no more LTS releases before 5.18.
  4. Flatpak: Runtime 26.08 for arm64 and x86_64
  5. MacOS. Universal builds targeting 10.10
  6. Android: 32-bit and 64 bit builds , 32-bits still mandated by Google (?).

All platform uses wxWidgets 3.2 except:

- Windows (win64) uses 3.3 or, if available when released, 3.4.
- Android uses 3.0.

Overall update to wxWidgets 3.4 is planned for 5.18.
A message was moved here from #Master > Using wxwidgets 3.3 on Windows by Alec Leamas.

From now on the only Win package on CL is for W-64.
This means that users who want to test changes and fixes cannot use any external plugins. (Except xGrib) What is the plan for all external plugins for Windows 64? I assume someone has to rebuild them? (I may have missed some info, so please..)
Plugins needs to be rebuilt for 5.16 for multiple reasons, win64 one of them. First thing is updating opencpn-libs and shipdriver, in place for master but not released yet.
I have already updated opencpn-libs and ShipDriver_pi template for that, so nothing blocks the other pugins. Except 26.08 flatpak which I think is still not implemented in ShipDriver

Android:

  1. I have dropped new builds for ARMHF (32 bits) as of July, 2026. Demand has fallen to near zero. Last good 32 bit build is still available on the Playstore for those few legacy users.
  2. Expecting to use wx3.3/3.4 for Android on 5.16.

Plugins needs to be rebuilt for 5.16

By whom? Each and every plugin author or?
If the respective publisher is going to rebuild, there are probably plugins that will not be available for x64 because the author is no longer available?
But maybe it's an accepted consequence of the development for the future?

Plugins needs to be rebuilt more or less for every opencpn release for various reasons, this is not that dramatic. Last time this happened for win32 was the wxwidgets 3.0 -> 3.2 transition.

That is, I doubt there is any plugin in the catalog which is not maintained and thus won't be rebuilt.
